reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Mixing classes from the modified version.
name: Raymond-Roy Occlusion Classification

version.label: Raymond-Roy occlusion classification (Raymond et al. 2003)
version.detail: Classes I–III. The modified classification (Mascitelli et al. 2015) splits class III into IIIa and IIIb and is a different version.

purpose: Classifies the angiographic occlusion of an aneurysm after coil embolisation.
intendedPopulation: Patients with intracranial aneurysms treated with coils, at treatment and follow-up.

options.label: Complete obliteration
options.detail: No contrast filling of the aneurysm sac or neck at this assessment.

options.label: Residual neck
options.detail: Contrast filling of the neck only.

options.label: Residual aneurysm
options.detail: Contrast filling of the aneurysm sac.

resultStates.label: Complete obliteration
resultStates.summary: No contrast filling of the aneurysm sac or neck at this assessment.

resultStates.label: Residual neck
resultStates.summary: Contrast filling of the neck only.

resultStates.label: Residual aneurysm
resultStates.summary: Contrast filling of the aneurysm sac.

clinicalContext.text: Standard description of coil occlusion, used to judge recurrence risk and follow-up.

clinicalInsights.text: Residual aneurysm is associated with higher recurrence; the modified classification distinguishes contrast within the coil mass (IIIa) from along the wall (IIIb).

limitations.text: Two-dimensional angiographic assessment; small remnants may be missed.

limitations: Not designed for flow diverters or intrasaccular devices.

guideSections.what: Three classes of aneurysm occlusion after coiling.
guideSections.whenToUse: Immediately after coiling and at angiographic follow-up.
guideSections.howToPerform: On working projections, assess contrast in the neck and sac; choose the class.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Guides surveillance in combination with aneurysm features.

sources.citation: Raymond J, Guilbert F, Weill A, et al. Long-term angiographic recurrences after selective endovascular treatment of aneurysms with detachable coils. Stroke. 2003;34(6):1398-1403.
Roy D, Milot G, Raymond J. Endovascular treatment of unruptured aneurysms. Stroke. 2001;32(9):1998-2004.
